title: USGS SIM 3292 Chronostratigraphic System of Mars
authors: Kenneth L. Tanaka, James A. Skinner Jr., James M. Dohm, et al. (2014)

epochs.name: Late Amazonian
epochs.climate: Hyper-arid, cold desert, low atmospheric pressure (~600 Pa), dominated by eolian activity and obliquity-driven ice mobilization.

survival_implications.trafficability: Extreme caution around active dune fields (lAd) which pose wheel sinkage traps; smooth volcanic plains provide excellent travel corridors.
survival_implications.isru_water: Highest near-surface pure water ice abundance in lobate debris aprons and polar caps.
survival_implications.radiation: Lava tubes in Tharsis/Elysium provide 100% cosmic ray and solar storm shielding.

epochs.name: Middle Amazonian
epochs.climate: Hyper-arid cold desert with periodic glacial deposition during high-obliquity cycles.

survival_implications.trafficability: Generally favorable across northern lowland plains.
survival_implications.isru_water: Buried permafrost ice within upper 1-3 meters.
survival_implications.radiation: Requires sintered regolith shielding or subterranean habitats.

epochs.name: Early Amazonian
epochs.climate: Transition to hyper-aridity, cessation of major surface water, giant shield volcano growth.
major_processes: Emplacement of massive shield volcanoes (Olympus Mons, Tharsis Montes)

survival_implications.trafficability: Steep volcanic slopes require tracked/tethered rovers; surrounding basalt flows provide flat routes.

epochs.name: Late Hesperian
epochs.climate: Arid with episodic catastrophic releases of groundwater forming giant outflow channels and transient lakes/seas.

survival_implications.trafficability: Optimal high-speed traverse terrain across flat flood basalts (lHv) and lowland polygonal plains (lHl).
survival_implications.isru_water: Polyhydrated sulfates, gypsum, and cryogenic ice in delta deposits.
survival_implications.radiation: Dense basaltic regolith provides high-efficiency gamma ray attenuation.

epochs.name: Early Hesperian
epochs.climate: Cooling, drying, and acidifying aqueous environment; decline of valley networks; onset of global catastrophic flood volcanism.
major_processes: Global flood basalts with wrinkle ridges (eHv)

survival_implications.trafficability: Flood basalts are ideal; chaotic collapse zones are impassable.
survival_implications.isru_water: Hydrated sulfate minerals release water at relatively low temperatures (150-300°C).
survival_implications.radiation: Abundant sulfur for sulfur-based concrete and structural masonry.

epochs.name: Late Noachian
epochs.climate: Warm and wet or cold and icy with transient melting; dense atmosphere; active hydrological cycle with rainfall/snowmelt and persistent lakes.
major_processes: Lacustrine open-basin crater lakes (Jezero crater delta formation)

survival_implications.trafficability: Moderately rugged; crater rims and boulder-strewn slopes require careful path planning.
survival_implications.isru_water: Phyllosilicates (smectite clays) contain 5-10% chemically bound water recoverable by microwave heating.
survival_implications.radiation: Natural shielding in deep crater floors and canyon walls.

epochs.name: Middle Noachian
epochs.climate: Substantial atmosphere, extensive aqueous alteration under neutral-to-alkaline pH conditions.
major_processes: Subsurface hydrothermal alteration producing Fe/Mg smectites and carbonates

survival_implications.trafficability: Rugged highland plateaus with significant obstacles.
survival_implications.isru_water: Carbonates and hydrated silicates offer industrial feedstock and water.
survival_implications.radiation: Clay-rich regolith can be pressed and sintered into dense radiation shelter blocks.

epochs.name: Early Noachian
epochs.climate: Planetary accretion aftermath, Late Heavy Bombardment, active core dynamo and global magnetic field.

survival_implications.trafficability: Steepest and most rugged terrain on Mars; accessible only via aerial/sub-orbital reconnaissance.
survival_implications.radiation: High natural topographic shielding within deep basin floors.
